note.question: How do index policies and performance bounds interact for dynamic selection problems?
note.overview: The model considers dynamic selection problems, where a decision maker repeatedly selects a set of items from a larger collection of available items. A classic example is the dynamic assortment problem with demand learning, where a retailer chooses items to offer for sale subject to a display space constraint. The retailer may adjust the assortment over time in response to the observed demand.

A classic example is the dynamic assortment problem with demand learning, where a retailer chooses items to offer for sale subject to a display space constraint.

source.section: Dynamic Assortment Problem with Demand Learning
source.quote: Although Caro and Gallien (2007) modeled aggregate demand for a retailer over the course of a ﬁxed time period (say, a week), recent work on dynamic assortment problems have modeled the arrivals of in- dividual customers, for example, to a web page.
The retailer may adjust the assortment over time in response to the observed demand.
These dynamic selection problems are naturally formulated as stochastic dynamic programs (DPs) but are difficult to solve because the optimal selection decisions depend on the states of all items.
